author: cmungall
body:
https://www.uniprot.org/locations/SL-0304
Cellular component - Cilium axoneme

has no GO mappings

should correspond to this:

```yaml
id: GO:0005930
name: axoneme
def: "The bundle of microtubules and associated proteins that forms the core of cilia (also called flagella) in eukaryotic cells and is responsible for their movements." [GOC:bf, GOC:cilia, ISBN:0198547684]
xref: Wikipedia:Axoneme
subset: goslim_pir
synonym: "ciliary axoneme" EXACT []
synonym: "cilium axoneme" EXACT []
synonym: "flagellar axoneme" EXACT []
synonym: "flagellum axoneme" EXACT []
relationship: BFO:0000050 GO:0005856 ! cytoskeleton
relationship: BFO:0000050 GO:0097014 ! ciliary plasm
relationship: BFO:0000051 GO:0005874 ! microtubule
relationship: RO:0002162 NCBITaxon:2759 ! Eukaryota
is_a: GO:0110165 ! cellular anatomical structure
```

Aside:

I noticed this missing mapping when I looked at the entry for human CFAP300. This is a well studied conserved protein with strong experimental, phylogenetic, phenotypic, and proteomic evidence for a ciliary function.

I was surprised when I saw no GO annotations or link to QuickGO in the place I am used to seeing them:
https://www.uniprot.org/uniprotkb/Q9BRQ4/entry

It looks like if I want to see GO cc annotations I need to scroll down to the subcellular section (is this a new thing), and click on the GO tab. Even here the GO annotations are weak, but I saw the KW/SL and was surprised it hadn't propagated.
title: Missing UniProt SL mapping: https://www.uniprot.org/locations/SL-0304 to axoneme

author: Antonialock
body: sl-0304 was mapped to GO:0035085 which is a secondary ID to  GO:0005930 - I didn't know secondary IDs aren't allowed. I've updated the mapping and have alook at the logs for more of these, thanks.
